column1: # The P3 row set (plan R0, frozen 2026-10-17; ADR 0013, ADR 0014, verification.md 3.3).
# kaluza-sim's own ksim-p3.* rows only. The P1 and P2 rows stay in p1.tsv and p2.tsv; P3 scores
# them again in its topologies (p3_exit's regression part, plan R21).
#   p3          yes for every row here (anything else becomes a v1.x or P4 row)
#   cores       stub, open5gs, kaluza, uesim (as in P2). open5gs=allow: an Open5GS deviation is
#               allowed with a reference (gates/allow/open5gs.tsv). kaluza=gap: CORE_GAP, the
#               procedure is one kaluza-core's register lists as unserved today (its AMF serves no
#               handover, one AMF, TAC 000001 only, no SUCI keys or 999/70 seed yet); the row is
#               named, never counted, until wave 40's roll serves it (D1, D5; design point g)
#   modes       aio, split (as in P2); C6 (OCUDU's CU-CP and CU-UP with two of our DUs), C7 (Xn
#               between our gNB and a C3-shaped OCUDU gNB), C8 (N2 between the same pair), ADR 0014
#   topology    1g: one gNB, one DU (the P1/P2 topologies); 1g2d: one gNB, two DUs of one cell each
#               (D7); 3g: three gNBs of two DUs each, Xn mesh (design point a); oc: our gNB beside
#               OCUDU's; 3g7: 3g with the third gNB's cells on TAC 000007
#   milestone   where the row is first scored (R3..R20). R2's rows and R3's cell-off-on are
#               scored from R4, whose topologies run one gNB with two DUs; until then the
#   mutant      the KSIM_MUTATIONS switch that must fail the row ('-': interop rows, whose control
#               is the peer; measured rows, whose control is the number; fault rows, whose control
#   evidence    what the gate reads; clause cites per row in the text's spec column
